posts.text:
New flagstone patio by the pool in Hallsville, TX.

This family wanted a spot to sit around a fire at night now that summer is winding down, so our crew built a rounded flagstone patio off the end of their pool deck.

We started with chopped stone borders, set by hand to a string line and checked with a level so the edge stays true. Inside the border went a crushed limestone base, raked out solid and even. The flagstone they picked went on top, with every piece fit by hand and the joints filled.

See the video and every photo from this job on our site.

posts.text:
New sprinkler system and Bermuda sod in Longview, TX.

This yard had more dirt than grass. Our crew trenched across it for the irrigation pipe, cutting through concrete with a saw where a line had to cross, then set the valves so each part of the yard waters on its own zone.

Track loaders brought in about 30 yards of topsoil and spread it evenly. About 32 sprinkler heads went in and the system was tested. Last came 19 pallets of Bermuda sod, laid by hand piece by piece. Installs are done under a Texas Licensed Irrigator.

See the video and every photo from this job on our site.

posts.text:
New 90-foot flagstone walkway with path lights in Kilgore, TX.

This homeowner wanted one solid path tying the house to the back porch, ready to connect to whatever they build next. Our crew spread a crushed limestone base with a track loader and compacted it with a plate compactor.

Chopped stone borders were shaped, mortared and set by hand down both sides, then flagstone filled the space between them, fit piece by piece. Two new flower beds went in along the walkway with six azaleas. To finish, we ran electrical wire along both sides up to the back porch and set path lights along the way.

See the video and every photo from this job on our site.

posts.text:
New flagstone seating area in Kilgore, TX.

We built this homeowner a flagstone walkway with path lights in September, and they reached back out to add a round patio seating area right off it.

Like all our flagstone patios, it starts with a chopped stone border set around the shape. Crushed limestone goes in next and is compacted into a solid base. Then the flagstone is fit piece by piece, set in mortar, and every joint is filled by hand. The new seating area ties right into the walkway and path lights.

See the video and every photo from this job on our site.

posts.text:
New raised boat and RV pad in White Oak, TX.

The ground beside this homeowner's shed didn't line up with the building, so there was no level spot to park a boat or RV right up to it. Our crew fixed that with a raised pad.

Pressure-treated timbers were cut, set and leveled course by course to build a retaining wall along the pad line. Drainage fabric went down along the wall, then dirt was hauled in with a track loader to fill it and compacted with a plate compactor so the pad holds its shape. Crushed concrete went on top and was raked out level across the whole pad.

See the video and every photo from this job on our site.

posts.text:
Weekly lawn care on one of our routes around Longview, TX.

Most of what our crews do every week is lawn care. The same crew works the same yards on the same day, so they know every gate, bed and tricky corner.

On each visit, stand-on and walk-behind mowers cut the front and back yards at the right height for the grass. String trimmers get along the house and the fence, and walks, drives and curbs get a clean edge. Before the crew leaves, clippings are blown off every walk, drive and patio. We run weekly or every-other-week visits in Longview and nearby towns.

See the video and every photo from this route on our site.

posts.text:
How we built a flagstone fire patio by the pool in Hallsville, TX.

This family wanted a place for nightly campfires now that the evenings are cooler. Here's how the crew got it done, start to finish.

A track loader cut out the rounded shape at the end of the pool deck, and the old turf and dirt went out in the dump trailer. Chopped stone borders went in next, each stone set by hand to a string line and checked with a level. Crushed limestone was spread inside the border and raked into a solid, even base. Last, the flagstone the homeowners picked was fit piece by piece and the joints were filled.

See the video and every photo from this job on our site.

posts.text:
Full deck repair under way in White Oak, TX.

This deck had busted boards, worn-out steps and a railing that had to come off, so our crew took it back to the frame to rebuild it.

The old railing came off first so the crew could see every post and board underneath. The worn steps were taken apart down to the framing. Rotted and split boards were pried up and the nails pulled, and new boards go in where they came out. Then come new steps, new railing across the whole deck, and a fresh restain and paint so it all matches.

See every photo from this job on our site.

posts.text:
New river rock flower bed and Christmas lights in Longview, TX.

This front bed was cleared out to bare ground and rebuilt as a clean, low-maintenance river rock bed. Landscape fabric went down first to keep weeds out, then river rock went over it with a few larger boulders set in. The new shrubs were set out in their pots to check the spacing before planting: Indian hawthorns, Sunshine Ligustrum and Texas Sage, a mix that handles East Texas heat with very little upkeep. For each one the crew pulled back the rock, cut an opening in the fabric, planted it and pulled the rock back around it.

The same home got warm white C9 bulbs clipped along the gutters and eaves across the front of the house for the season.

See more photos from this bed and lights job on our site.

posts.text:
Behind the scenes on a Longview, TX irrigation and Bermuda sod job.

Before any grass went down, the crew dug trenches across the yard for the irrigation pipe and set the valves so every section of the lawn runs on its own zone. Then the track loaders went to work, hauling in roughly 30 yards of topsoil and leveling it out across the whole yard.

With the ground ready, about 32 sprinkler heads were installed and tested, and 19 pallets of Bermuda sod were laid by hand on top. Doing it in that order means nothing gets dug back up once the new lawn is in.

See the video and every photo from this job on our site.
